finding.text: The new "Your prompts" pinned row says only "You said..." dated Oct 1, though the owner's prompt that started this task came at 21:03 on Oct 2. Its one line tells the reader nothing and looks out of date (page 8; requirement 5). Evidence: shots/…-ai2/1200.png, rail, first row.

Each card on the "Your prompts" page is built with `sentences: null, structured: null` (`ai2/faces.js` `prompt_timeline_row`). So Condensed, Structured and Clean all show the same fallback text, and the four modes the owner asked for show nothing different from each other yet (requirement 5).

Dictate still runs its own clean step, and live Dictate plays no sound on a red flag. This diff doesn't touch `ux/Dictate`, so requirements 1 and 4 are only half met here. The brief gives that work to @task-mastermind-one-dictation, so it needs a link to that task before this one can count as landed.

The litmus sample was chosen because it had "a real mid-sentence self-correction", but all three models came back with `strikes: 0`. So `detectStrikes()` missed the one correction it was tested on (requirement 2a). Source: Server/refine-litmus-result.json.

The litmus pick is less solid than its verdict line makes it sound. Haiku cost $0.15 and took 123 s for 79 words. The two OpenRouter costs are rough estimates priced from Anthropic's table, as the doc itself warns. "Cheapest wins" therefore compares figures that weren't measured the same way (requirement 7).
The review shots are of the `/framework/ai2/` index only. The new view, `/framework/ai2/your-prompts/`, wasn't shot, so the prompt card and its mode tabs have no visual proof.
Switching a card's mode doesn't change the URL, so a reload drops back to Condensed (page 6). The comment in `prompt-card.js` still calls the engine `refine.js`, but the file is now `engine.js`.
